note: Anti-IL-13 antibodies (tralokinumab, lebrikizumab, GSK679586, dectrekumab) went into asthma on IL-13-blockade mouse models and a cynomolgus antigen challenge; lebrikizumab raised FEV1 in periostin-high patients in phase 2, but every phase 3 exacerbation endpoint (LAVOLTA, STRATOS) was missed and no member was approved for asthma.
label: Asthma (anti-IL-13)

engagement.note: Soluble IL-13Ralpha2-Fc abolished allergen-induced AHR and mucus in OVA mice; readouts were AHR, mucus and BAL eosinophils.
engagement.quote: IL-13 induces the pathophysiological features of asthma in a manner that is independent of immunoglobulin E and eosinophils.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The companion paper Grunig 1998 (doi:10.1126/science.282.5397.2261) reported that IL-13 neutralisation also reduced eosinophil recruitment.
engagement.judgement: Opens the class strip with the two Science papers that made IL-13 the target; they disagree on eosinophils (Wills-Karp: independent; Grunig: reduced), which matters for the 2018 comparison.

engagement.model: IL-13-stimulated bronchial epithelial cells and patient brushings (periostin signature)
engagement.note: IL-13 induced CLCA1, periostin and SERPINB2 in cultured airway epithelium; the same genes marked a Th2-high subgroup in patient brushings.
engagement.short: IL-13 signature genes in patient epithelium
engagement.quote: By using airway epithelial cells in culture, we found that IL-13 increased expression of CLCA1, periostin, and serpinB2, an effect that was suppressed by corticosteroids.
engagement.judgement: A patient-derived ex-vivo system whose readout (the IL-13 epithelial signature, later serum periostin) became the pharmacodynamic and selection marker for the class; scored as its own track at prediction_level patient.

engagement.note: Tralokinumab (CAT-354) inhibited AHR and BAL eosinophilia after antigen challenge in cynomolgus monkeys and in IL-13-humanised OVA mice. Dated to the online publication (2011-09-08), the earliest public date.
engagement.short: Tralokinumab cuts monkey AHR and BAL eosinophils
engagement.quote: In vivo in humanized mouse and cynomolgus monkey antigen challenge models CAT-354 inhibited airways hyperresponsiveness and bronchoalveolar lavage eosinophilia.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Filed in the atopic-dermatitis BLA 761180 (the FDA integrated review lists the cynomolgus antigen-challenge study CAT354Rp038), not in an asthma filing.
engagement.judgement: The only member tested in a non-rodent disease model; a different system from the OVA mouse (natural sensitisation, primate IL-13), so it carries its own track.

engagement.model: IL-13-stimulated bronchial epithelial cells and patient brushings (periostin signature)
engagement.note: GSK679586 (single IV doses) cut FeNO 19-52% dose-dependently in mild asthmatics and raised total serum IL-13 (drug-target complexes).
engagement.quote: mean levels of exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO), a marker of pulmonary inflammation, were reduced relative to baseline at 2.5, 10 and 20 mg kg(-1) doses of GSK679586 at both 2 weeks (19%, 44% and 52% decreases)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only. FeNO (epithelial iNOS) is an IL-13-driven epithelial readout but not the periostin/CLCA1/SERPINB2 signature itself; serum CCL13/CCL17 falls with lebrikizumab (Scheerens 2014, doi:10.1111/cea.12220) were read at abstract level. PubMed indexed the paper in May 2012, so an early-view 2012 date is likely but unverified.
engagement.judgement: Scored same because the epithelial IL-13 readout moved in dosed asthmatics in the predicted direction at every active dose; no source states the comparison, so it is a pairing. MESOS 2018 (FeNO ratio 0.78, p=0.023) and LAVOLTA 2016 ('blocked interleukin-13 as evidenced by the effect on interleukin-13-related pharmacodynamic biomarkers') confirm without changing status.
engagement.reason: FeNO and Th2 chemokines fell as predicted
engagement.magnitude_basis: FeNO change from baseline; the signature genes themselves were not measured

engagement.note: MESOS: tralokinumab 300 mg q2w left bronchial, sputum and blood eosinophils unchanged (bronchial ratio 1.43) while FeNO and IgE fell.
engagement.quote: Tralokinumab did not significantly affect eosinophilic inflammation in bronchial submucosa, blood, or sputum compared with placebo, but did reduce FENO and IgE concentrations.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only (n=79, 12 weeks). The mouse literature is split: Wills-Karp 1998 said IL-13 acts independently of eosinophils; Grunig 1998 and the IL-13-humanised OVA mouse in May 2012 said blockade reduces eosinophil recruitment. Scored against the latter because that is what the product's own package predicted.
engagement.judgement: Contra rather than untested because the eosinophil readout the models used was measured in patients at the phase-3 regimen and did not move; AHR and mucus, the other mouse readouts, were never measured as PD endpoints in a member trial. Authors' own conclusion: IL-13 'is not crucial for eosinophilic airway inflammation control'.
engagement.reason: Eosinophil readout did not move in patients
engagement.magnitude_basis: bronchial eosinophil treatment-effect ratio 1.43 (95% CI 0.63-3.27) against inhibition in the model

engagement.note: Monkey model predicted BAL eosinophilia falls with tralokinumab; MESOS found no eosinophil change in bronchial submucosa, sputum or blood at 300 mg q2w.
engagement.short: Monkey BAL eosinophil fall not seen in patients
engagement.quote: Tralokinumab did not significantly affect eosinophilic inflammation in bronchial submucosa, blood, or sputum compared with placebo, but did reduce FENO and IgE concentrations.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only (n=79, 12 weeks); the same product was dosed in the model and in the trial, so this is the cleanest model-to-patient PD pairing in the class.
engagement.judgement: Same comparison as the mouse track, scored separately because the monkey is a different system; FeNO and IgE did fall, so IL-13 was neutralised and the miss is on the readout the model chose, not on exposure.
engagement.reason: BAL eosinophil prediction failed in patients
engagement.magnitude_basis: bronchial eosinophil treatment-effect ratio 1.43 (95% CI 0.63-3.27) against inhibition in the model

engagement.model: IL-13-humanised OVA-sensitised mouse dosed with tralokinumab
engagement.note: Tralokinumab reduced AHR and BAL eosinophilia after OVA challenge in mice carrying human IL-13; the readouts were AHR and BAL eosinophils.
engagement.short: Tralokinumab cuts humanised-mouse AHR and eosinophils
engagement.quote: In vivo in humanized mouse and cynomolgus monkey antigen challenge models CAT-354 inhibited airways hyperresponsiveness and bronchoalveolar lavage eosinophilia.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; online 2011-09-08 (PubMed), print May 2012. The FDA BLA 761180 integrated review lists the study as CAT354Rp043 (BALB/c male mice).
engagement.judgement: A genetically distinct system from Wills-Karp's wild-type OVA mouse: tralokinumab does not bind mouse IL-13, so the product was dosed only here, and this system states eosinophil reduction where the wild-type system stated eosinophil-independence. Opens at the online date.

engagement.model: IL-13-humanised OVA-sensitised mouse dosed with tralokinumab
engagement.note: MESOS: tralokinumab 300 mg q2w left bronchial, sputum and blood eosinophils unchanged (bronchial ratio 1.43) while FeNO and IgE fell.
engagement.quote: Tralokinumab did not significantly affect eosinophilic inflammation in bronchial submucosa, blood, or sputum compared with placebo, but did reduce FENO and IgE concentrations.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only (n=79, 12 weeks); registry date is the MESOS results posting. AHR, the model's other readout, was never measured as a PD endpoint in a member trial.
engagement.judgement: The product itself, at the phase 3 regimen, did not reproduce the eosinophil reduction its own mouse package predicted; FeNO and IgE moved, so this is a wrong readout prediction rather than a failure of target neutralisation.
engagement.reason: Eosinophil readout did not move in patients
engagement.magnitude_basis: bronchial eosinophil treatment-effect ratio 1.43 (95% CI 0.63-3.27) against inhibition of BAL eosinophilia in the model

engagement.model: Mathematical model of blood and airway eosinophil dynamics under anti-IL-13 therapy
engagement.note: A QSP model of eosinophil dynamics predicted lebrikizumab/tralokinumab raise blood eosinophils (30%/10%) while lowering airway eosinophils.
engagement.short: QSP model: blood eosinophils up, airway down
engagement.quote: For the anti-IL-13 therapies, lebrikizumab and tralokinumab, the model predicted an increase of 30% and 10% in total and activated EOS in the blood, respectively, and a decrease in the total and activated EOS in the airways.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; PubMed date 2016-11-26, print November 2016. The model was built after the phase 2 blood-eosinophil observations it reproduces.
engagement.judgement: Opens the in-silico eosinophil track at its first use; the same paper then states the comparison (next entry).

engagement.model: Mathematical model of blood and airway eosinophil dynamics under anti-IL-13 therapy
engagement.note: The paper sets its predicted 10% blood-eosinophil rise with tralokinumab beside the published phase 2 eosinophil data and calls them consistent.
engagement.quote: All model-based predictions were consistent with published clinical observations.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only; which clinical datasets were used is not visible at abstract level.
engagement.judgement: A retrodiction: built after the clinic had seen blood eosinophils rise on anti-IL-13 antibodies, so retro, never same (decision 10).
engagement.magnitude_basis: blood eosinophil change: model +10% (tralokinumab) against published phase 2 observations (values not in the abstract)

engagement.model: Mathematical model of blood and airway eosinophil dynamics under anti-IL-13 therapy
engagement.note: MESOS: the model's prospective prediction of lower airway eosinophils failed; tralokinumab left bronchial submucosal and sputum eosinophils unchanged.
engagement.quote: Tralokinumab did not significantly affect eosinophilic inflammation in bronchial submucosa, blood, or sputum compared with placebo, but did reduce FENO and IgE concentrations.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only (n=79); subgroup figures (blood ratio 1.21, p=0.055; sputum 0.57, p=0.63) are from the published results as recorded by the checker, not re-read here. The blood half of the prediction is not contradicted; the airway half is.
engagement.judgement: The model's first prospective prediction after the retrodiction (decision 10): airway eosinophils were measured in MESOS and did not fall, so the track turns contra.
engagement.reason: Airway eosinophil prediction failed in MESOS
engagement.magnitude_basis: bronchial eosinophil treatment-effect ratio 1.43 (95% CI 0.63-3.27) and sputum 0.57 (p=0.63) against a predicted decrease

engagement.model: IL-13-stimulated bronchial epithelial cells and patient brushings (periostin signature)
engagement.note: IL-13 induced CLCA1, periostin and SERPINB2 in cultured airway epithelium; the same genes marked a Th2-high subgroup in patient brushings.
engagement.short: IL-13 signature genes in patient epithelium
engagement.quote: By using airway epithelial cells in culture, we found that IL-13 increased expression of CLCA1, periostin, and serpinB2, an effect that was suppressed by corticosteroids.
engagement.judgement: Opener of the lebrikizumab track on the epithelial-signature model at the model's first use (2007).

engagement.model: IL-13-stimulated bronchial epithelial cells and patient brushings (periostin signature)
engagement.note: Lebrikizumab 5 mg/kg sc q4w cut serum IgE, CCL13 and CCL17 by about 25% in 29 mild allergic asthmatics, the Th2 readouts the signature model predicts.
engagement.quote: Lebrikizumab exerted systemic effects on markers of Th2 inflammation, reducing serum immunoglobulin E (IgE), chemokine ligands 13 and 17 by approximately 25% (P < 0.01).
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 24131304); online 2013-10-18, print January 2014. LAVOLTA 2016 confirms ('it blocked interleukin-13 as evidenced by the effect on interleukin-13-related pharmacodynamic biomarkers').
engagement.judgement: Split from entry 4, whose note also covered lebrikizumab: the IL-13 downstream readouts moved in dosed patients, as the model predicted.
engagement.magnitude_basis: serum IgE, CCL13, CCL17 about -25%; signature genes not measured

engagement.model: IL-13-stimulated bronchial epithelial cells and patient brushings (periostin signature)
engagement.note: IL-13 induced CLCA1, periostin and SERPINB2 in cultured airway epithelium; the same genes marked a Th2-high subgroup in patient brushings.
engagement.short: IL-13 signature genes in patient epithelium
engagement.quote: By using airway epithelial cells in culture, we found that IL-13 increased expression of CLCA1, periostin, and serpinB2, an effect that was suppressed by corticosteroids.
engagement.judgement: Opener of the tralokinumab track on the epithelial-signature model at the model's first use (2007).

engagement.model: IL-13-stimulated bronchial epithelial cells and patient brushings (periostin signature)
engagement.note: MESOS: tralokinumab 300 mg q2w lowered FeNO and IgE, the IL-13-driven epithelial and Th2 readouts, though eosinophils did not fall.
engagement.short: FeNO and IgE fell with tralokinumab
engagement.quote: Tralokinumab did not significantly affect eosinophilic inflammation in bronchial submucosa, blood, or sputum compared with placebo, but did reduce FENO and IgE concentrations.
engagement.judgement: Split from entry 4 (its judgement cited MESOS): on the signature model's own readouts the product moved FeNO, so same; the eosinophil miss belongs to the animal tracks.
engagement.magnitude_basis: FeNO treatment ratio 0.78 (p=0.023) per the draft's MESOS reading; signature genes not measured
engagement.reason: FeNO fell as the signature predicted

engagement.model: Mathematical model of blood and airway eosinophil dynamics under anti-IL-13 therapy
engagement.note: A QSP model of eosinophil dynamics predicted lebrikizumab/tralokinumab raise blood eosinophils (30%/10%) while lowering airway eosinophils.
engagement.short: QSP model: blood eosinophils up, airway down
engagement.quote: For the anti-IL-13 therapies, lebrikizumab and tralokinumab, the model predicted an increase of 30% and 10% in total and activated EOS in the blood, respectively, and a decrease in the total and activated EOS in the airways.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; PubMed date 2016-11-26, print November 2016. The model was built after the phase 2 blood-eosinophil observations it reproduces.
engagement.judgement: Opener of the lebrikizumab track on the eosinophil QSP model (split from entry 10).

engagement.model: Mathematical model of blood and airway eosinophil dynamics under anti-IL-13 therapy
engagement.note: The model's predicted 30% blood-eosinophil rise with lebrikizumab matched the published phase 2 observations it was built after.
engagement.quote: All model-based predictions were consistent with published clinical observations.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only; which clinical datasets were used is not visible at abstract level.
engagement.judgement: Split from entry 10, which covered both drugs; a retrodiction, so retro.
engagement.magnitude_basis: blood eosinophil change: model +30% (lebrikizumab) against published phase 2 observations

dose.note: The models set no human exposure target; tralokinumab 300 mg q2w came from phase 1/2 PK, total-IL-13 capture and FeNO, lebrikizumab 125 mg q4w likewise. Dated to the online publication (2011-09-08), the earliest public date.
dose.short: No exposure target from the models
dose.quote: CAT-354 has a 165 pM affinity for human IL-13 and functionally neutralized human, human variant associated with asthma and atopy (R130Q) and cynomolgus monkey, but not mouse, IL-13.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract only; the abstract reports potency and in-vivo efficacy but no exposure-response, so any target is inferred from the clinical PK/PD programme rather than stated by the model.
dose.judgement: Opens the dose strip on the only member whose animal pharmacology is published; lebrikizumab, GSK679586 and dectrekumab have no published animal PK/PD, so they ride this track only through the class-level comparison below.

dose.model: Integrated population PK/PD dose-exposure-FEV1 model of tralokinumab (phase 2a/2b data)
dose.note: A population PK/PD model pooling phase 2a/2b data predicted near-maximal FEV1 at 300 mg q2w and set the phase 3 regimen.
dose.short: Model picked 300 mg q2w for phase 3
dose.quote: Near-maximal FEV1 increase was predicted at a dose of 300 mg SC once every 2 weeks (Q2W).
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; epub 2017-09-28, print May 2018. The model was built for phase 3 dose selection before the STRATOS results (registry 2018-03-21), so its prediction was prospective. Not found in the tralokinumab FDA review (BLA 761180, atopic dermatitis).
dose.judgement: A separate in-silico system from the cynomolgus track: the only member model that stated a human regimen target. Opens untested at its online date.

dose.model: Integrated population PK/PD dose-exposure-FEV1 model of tralokinumab (phase 2a/2b data)
dose.note: 300 mg q2w, the model's near-maximal FEV1 dose, was given in STRATOS 1/2. The model was first public (2017) after STRATOS 1 had been announced (2017-05-10), so it is a retrodiction: the regimen it chose had already been reached.
dose.short: Model's 300 mg q2w reached; FEV1 moved
dose.quote: In the STRATOS 1 all-comers population, tralokinumab every 2 weeks did not significantly reduce AAER compared with placebo (7·0% reduction [95% CI -20·8 to 28·4]; rate ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·72 to 1·21]; p=0·59).
dose.confidence_note: Abstract only. The model predicted FEV1, not exacerbations; STRATOS FEV1 secondaries are not in the abstract, so the contra is derived from the primary-endpoint failure under the dose table (reached, failed, abandoned).
dose.judgement: Post-dating ruling: a model first public after a same-target patient result is a retrodiction; the dose it stated was reached, so retro, not same.
dose.magnitude_basis: AAER rate ratio 0.93 at the model-selected 300 mg q2w

dose.model: Integrated population PK/PD dose-exposure-FEV1 model of tralokinumab (phase 2a/2b data)
dose.note: 300 mg q2w, the model's near-maximal FEV1 dose, was given in STRATOS 1/2; both exacerbation primaries missed and asthma development stopped. A retrodiction: the model was first public after STRATOS 1 was announced (2017-05-10); dated to that announcement.
dose.quote: In the STRATOS 1 all-comers population, tralokinumab every 2 weeks did not significantly reduce AAER compared with placebo (7·0% reduction [95% CI -20·8 to 28·4]; rate ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·72 to 1·21]; p=0·59).
dose.confidence_note: Abstract only. The model predicted FEV1, not exacerbations; STRATOS FEV1 secondaries are not in the abstract, so the contra is derived from the primary-endpoint failure under the dose table (reached, failed, abandoned).
dose.judgement: Case 'reached, failed, abandoned': the regimen the model chose was tested and the programme ended; counted once, as a derived dose failure, with efficacy carried on the animal tracks.
dose.magnitude_basis: AAER rate ratio 0.93 at the model-selected 300 mg q2w

efficacy.model: OVA-sensitised mouse with IL-13 neutralisation
efficacy.note: Soluble IL-13Ralpha2-Fc reversed allergen-induced AHR and mucus in OVA mice; IL-13 alone reproduced the phenotype in naive mice.
efficacy.short: IL-13 necessary and sufficient in mice
efficacy.quote: The type 2 cytokine IL-13, which shares a receptor component and signaling pathways with IL-4, was found to be necessary and sufficient for the expression of allergic asthma.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; Grunig 1998 is the independent replication with a different neutralising reagent.
efficacy.judgement: The class-founding model; every member's rationale cites it. Tralokinumab is the only member later dosed in a mouse (IL-13-humanised OVA mouse, May 2012), so product_in_model turns true from 2012 on this track.

efficacy.model: IL-13-stimulated bronchial epithelial cells and patient brushings (periostin signature)
efficacy.note: Periostin, CLCA1 and SERPINB2 marked IL-13-driven epithelium in patient brushings; serum periostin became the selection marker for lebrikizumab.
efficacy.quote: By using gene expression microarrays, we found that chloride channel, calcium-activated, family member 1 (CLCA1), periostin, and serine peptidase inhibitor, clade B (ovalbumin), member 2 (serpinB2) were up-regulated in asthma but not in smokers.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; open access.
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level track: the prediction is who responds (IL-13-signature-high patients), not whether the class works.

efficacy.model: OVA-sensitised mouse with IL-13 neutralisation
efficacy.note: MILLY: lebrikizumab raised FEV1 5.5 points over placebo at week 12 (p=0.02) in 219 ICS-uncontrolled adults; exacerbations (secondary) did not fall.
efficacy.quote: At week 12, the mean increase in FEV(1) was 5.5 percentage points higher in the lebrikizumab group than in the placebo group (P = 0.02).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; NCT00930163 never posted results.
efficacy.judgement: The first member trial met its primary endpoint, so the mouse direction held for lung function; the 5.5-point gain is modest and exacerbations did not fall, which is why magnitude is direction_only.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: FEV1 (physiology) against mouse AHR; no common scale

patient_trials.quote: Lebrikizumab treatment was associated with improved lung function.

efficacy.model: IL-13-stimulated bronchial epithelial cells and patient brushings (periostin signature)
efficacy.note: Prespecified periostin-high subgroup gained 8.2 FEV1 points vs 1.6 in periostin-low with lebrikizumab (p=0.03 vs 0.61).
efficacy.short: Periostin-high patients responded, low did not
efficacy.quote: Among patients in the high-periostin subgroup, the increase from baseline FEV(1) was 8.2 percentage points higher in the lebrikizumab group than in the placebo group (P = 0.03).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; subgroup was prespecified and the trial was designed around the IL-13-signature hypothesis.
efficacy.judgement: comparison_stated true because the trial itself was built to test the signature model ('We hypothesized that anti-interleukin-13 therapy would benefit patients with asthma who had a pretreatment profile consistent with interleukin-13 activity') and reports the split; the model predicts who responds, not how much, so magnitude is direction_only.

patient_trials.quote: Patients with high pretreatment levels of serum periostin had greater improvement in lung function with lebrikizumab than did patients with low periostin levels.

efficacy.model: Cynomolgus monkey antigen challenge (tralokinumab)
efficacy.note: Tralokinumab inhibited AHR and BAL eosinophilia after antigen challenge in cynomolgus monkeys; the package was built for severe uncontrolled asthma. Dated to the online publication (2011-09-08), the earliest public date. The model became public after MILLY's lebrikizumab result; that retrodiction is scored on the lebrikizumab track appended below.
efficacy.quote: The preclinical data presented here support the trialling of this mAb in patients with moderate to severe uncontrolled asthma.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the FDA 2022 integrated review (BLA 761180) lists the study as CAT354Rp038.
efficacy.judgement: Separate track from the OVA mouse: a primate with natural Ascaris sensitisation dosed with the product itself.

efficacy.model: OVA-sensitised mouse with IL-13 neutralisation
efficacy.note: Tralokinumab phase 2a: ACQ-6 primary missed (-0.76 vs -0.61, p=0.375) in 194 moderate-severe asthmatics; FEV1 +0.15 L (p=0.072).
efficacy.quote: At week 13, change from baseline in ACQ-6 was -0.76±1.04 for tralokinumab versus -0.61±0.90 for placebo (p=0.375).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract only; a lung-function signal was present as a secondary, which a re-scorer could weigh as partial agreement. Epub 2012-06-27, print February 2013.
efficacy.judgement: Contra on the primary-endpoint rule; the authors call it mixed ('No improvement in ACQ-6 was observed, although tralokinumab treatment was associated with improved lung function'). Noonan 2013 (lebrikizumab, FEV1 primary missed in ICS-free asthma, epub 2013-05-29, doi:10.1016/j.jaci.2013.03.051) would date the contra a year later for a re-scorer who discounts symptom scores; the end state is the same.

patient_trials.quote: No improvement in ACQ-6 was observed, although tralokinumab treatment was associated with improved lung function.

efficacy.model: Cynomolgus monkey antigen challenge (tralokinumab)
efficacy.note: Weeks after the monkey package appeared, tralokinumab's phase 2a missed its ACQ-6 primary; lung function improved only as a secondary.
efficacy.quote: At week 13, change from baseline in ACQ-6 was -0.76±1.04 for tralokinumab versus -0.61±0.90 for placebo (p=0.375).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract only; same caveat as the mouse track (FEV1 secondary moved, dose-response seen).
efficacy.judgement: Same trial scored on the monkey track because the product was dosed in that model; the monkey predicted AHR relief, the trial's primary was a symptom score.

patient_trials.quote: No improvement in ACQ-6 was observed, although tralokinumab treatment was associated with improved lung function.

efficacy.model: IL-13-stimulated bronchial epithelial cells and patient brushings (periostin signature)
efficacy.note: Lebrikizumab 125-500 mg in 212 ICS-free asthmatics: FEV1 primary missed and no difference by periostin subgroup.
efficacy.short: Periostin did not pick responders off ICS
efficacy.quote: There were no meaningful differences in changes in FEV1 between the dose groups and the placebo group by the periostin subgroup.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract only; the population (no inhaled steroid) differs from MILLY, and protocol-defined treatment failure (a secondary) was reduced regardless of periostin. NCT00971035 never posted results.
efficacy.judgement: Contra because the patient-level prediction (periostin-high responds) failed on a primary endpoint; a re-scorer could date it to 2016 (LAVOLTA II, biomarker-high primary p=0.06) or 2018 (STRATOS 1 chose FeNO over periostin). LUTE/VERSE (Hanania 2015, exacerbations -60% periostin-high vs -5% low, doi:10.1136/thoraxjnl-2014-206719) supported the marker in between, but a contra on a track is not undone by a later same without patient_signal_reversed.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: FEV1 by periostin subgroup, no meaningful difference

patient_trials.quote: Blocking IL-13, a single cytokine, in this population of asthmatic patients is insufficient to improve lung function.

efficacy.model: OVA-sensitised mouse with IL-13 neutralisation
efficacy.note: GSK679586 10 mg/kg monthly: no change in ACQ (p=0.058), FEV1 (p=0.276) or exacerbations in 198 severe asthmatics, including IgE- or eosinophil-high patients.
efficacy.short: GSK679586 did nothing in severe asthma
efficacy.quote: Although well tolerated, GSK679586 did not demonstrate clinically meaningful improvements in asthma control, pulmonary function, or exacerbations in patients with severe asthma.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; no published animal model for GSK679586, so the mouse side is the class-founding paper.
efficacy.judgement: Second member failure on the same track. Dectrekumab (QAX576) ran a 259-patient asthma phase 2 (NCT01130064, completed 2012) that was never published or posted, so that member cannot be scored; its only published trial is in eosinophilic oesophagitis (Rothenberg 2015, doi:10.1016/j.jaci.2014.07.049). STRATOS 2018 (all-comers AAER rate ratio 0.93) later closed the class.
efficacy.reason: Mouse AHR benefit; patients did not respond
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ACQ difference 0.14 units, p=0.058; FEV1 p=0.276

patient_trials.quote: Incidence of asthma exacerbations was similar between treatments.

efficacy.model: Cynomolgus monkey antigen challenge (tralokinumab)
efficacy.note: Phase 2b: annual exacerbation rate 0.91 (q2w) and 0.97 (q4w) vs 0.90 on placebo in 452 severe asthmatics; FEV1 +7.3% at q2w only.
efficacy.quote: At week 52, percentage changes in annual asthma exacerbation rate were not significant with tralokinumab every 2 weeks or every 4 weeks versus placebo (6% [95% CI -31 to 33; p=0.709] and -2% [-46 to 29; p=0.904], respectively)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the post-hoc periostin/DPP-4 subgroup signals that motivated phase 3 are not in the abstract and were not scored.
efficacy.judgement: Primary missed at the regimen taken into phase 3, with the product that was dosed in the monkey; strengthens the 2012 contra rather than changing it.

patient_trials.quote: The annual asthma exacerbation rate at week 52 was similar between patients receiving tralokinumab every 2 weeks (0.91 per patient per year [95% CI 0.76-1.08]) and every 4 weeks (0.97 [0.81-1.14]), and those receiving placebo (0.90 [0.75-1.08]).

efficacy.model: IL-13-stimulated bronchial epithelial cells and patient brushings (periostin signature)
efficacy.note: Replicate phase 3s in biomarker-high patients (periostin >=50 ng/mL or eosinophils >=300/uL): LAVOLTA I rate ratios 0.49/0.70, LAVOLTA II 0.74/0.74 (p=0.06); Roche stopped.
efficacy.quote: Lebrikizumab did not consistently show significant reduction in asthma exacerbations in biomarker-high patients.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. LAVOLTA I results were posted to the registry only on 2026-07-17; LAVOLTA II never posted.
efficacy.judgement: Biomarker-high pooled periostin with blood eosinophils, so this is an imperfect test of the periostin model; STRATOS 1 (2018) then picked FeNO, not periostin, as tralokinumab's biomarker and STRATOS 2 failed to replicate even that. Authors leave it unresolved ('clinically relevant changes could not be ruled out').
efficacy.magnitude_basis: exacerbation rate ratio 0.74 (p=0.06) in LAVOLTA II biomarker-high

Scheerens' own conclusion is positive ('Lebrikizumab reduced the LAR in subjects with mild asthma') and it sets that beside MILLY's FEV1 gain in ICS-uncontrolled asthma (a same, listed under patient_trials); but the trial nearest the challenge population, ICS-free mild-to-moderate asthma, missed its FEV1 primary, and one contra outranks a same on a track.

safety.note: The monkey was the only pharmacologically relevant tox species (both antibodies neutralise cynomolgus but not mouse IL-13); tox findings stayed unpublished until the atopic-dermatitis filings. Dated to May 2012's online publication (2011-09-08).
safety.quote: In vivo CAT-354 was tested on human IL-13-induced air pouch inflammation in mice, ovalbumin-sensitization and challenge in IL-13 humanized mice and antigen challenge in cynomolgus monkeys.
safety.confidence_note: Proxy opening: the GLP monkey studies predate the 2006 phase 1 but their first public description is the FDA 2022 integrated review; May 2012 is cited only to date the species' use with the product.
safety.judgement: A separate track from the antigen-challenge monkey: naive animals, repeat dosing, toxicology endpoints.

safety.note: Monkey NOAEL 90-100 mg/kg/week with no immune or other findings; asthma pools were placebo-like (LAVOLTA SAEs 8% vs 9%, anaphylaxis 0.2% in both arms, one helminth infection in STRATOS 2). Asthma patients were measured, so their placebo-like safety sets the status and the atopic-dermatitis conjunctivitis is not imported. The monkey statement was first public in 2022, after the asthma safety data, so it is a retrodiction.
safety.short: Clean monkey tox; asthma safety placebo-like
safety.quote: No tralokinumab-related adverse effects (including effects on the immune system) were observed.
safety.confidence_note: The review's nonclinical statement and its asthma-pool AE searches (anaphylaxis, endoparasitosis) sit in one tier-2 document, but its clinical pool is atopic-dermatitis-centred, hence imported_from. Asthma-trial safety read at abstract level: Piper 2013 'no serious adverse events related to tralokinumab'; Hanania 2016 SAEs 8% vs 9%; Panettieri 2018 'consistent with that of previous tralokinumab trials'. Lebrikizumab's monkey NOAEL was likewise the highest dose tested (FDA BLA 761306 review, 2024).
safety.judgement: Imported-harm ruling: where this disease's patients were measured, their result sets the status, so the AD conjunctivitis excess is not imported (settles the checker's rule question 3). Post-dating ruling: the tox statement became public in 2022, after the asthma trials' safety, so retro rather than same.
safety.reason: No on-target harm, as monkeys predicted
